Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Environment: Warm temperatures (25–30°C), high humidity (>90%), prolonged leaf wetness and frequent rainfall.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Spread: Wind-borne spores, rain splash, infected crop residue and contaminated equipment.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Description: Gray Leaf Spot is one of the most economically important foliar diseases of maize. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis, weaken plants and significantly reduce grain yield.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small tan lesions appear between leaf veins.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions become rectangular and gray with distinct margins.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large portions of leaves become blighted, reducing photosynthesis.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually develop within 10–21 days after infection.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Environment: Cool to moderate temperatures (16–25°C), humid weather and frequent dew formation.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Spread: Wind-borne fungal spores travel long distances between maize fields.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Description: Common Rust is a widespread fungal disease characterized by reddish-brown pustules on maize leaves. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis and grain production.

Age_Cycle.Severe: Numerous pustules cover leaves causing reduced photosynthesis.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Disease develops within 7–14 days after infection.

Recommended_Actions: Apply fungicide when disease threshold is reached.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Environment: Moderate temperatures (18–27°C), high humidity, frequent rainfall and prolonged leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Spread: Airborne spores spread through wind, rain splash and infected crop residue.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Description: Northern Leaf Blight is a destructive foliar disease of maize that causes long cigar-shaped lesions on leaves. Severe infections reduce photosynthesis, weaken plants and significantly decrease grain yield.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small gray-green elliptical lesions appear on lower leaves.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Lesions expand into long cigar-shaped gray or tan patches.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Large portions of leaves become blighted, reducing grain filling and plant vigor.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually develop within 7–14 days after infection under favorable conditions.

Prevention: Remove infected crop residue after harvest.
Recommended_Actions: Apply fungicides before severe infection develops.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.Environment: Well-drained fertile soil, balanced fertilization, adequate sunlight and proper irrigation.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Description: The uploaded maize leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease, pest infestation or nutrient deficiency. The crop appears healthy and capable of normal growth and grain production.

Age_Cycle.Early: Healthy leaf emergence with uniform green color.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: Normal vegetative growth and canopy development.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Continuous healthy development throughout the growing season.

Organic_Treatment: Apply balanced organic fertilizers when necessary.
Recommended_Actions: Inspect plants weekly for early disease symptoms.
